claim: Epi-ID is a strategy to directly assess chromatin status in thousands of mutants by chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by deep sequencing.
source: Here we describe a strategy, Epi-ID, to directly assess chromatin status in thousands of mutants. In Epi-ID, chromatin status on DNA barcodes is interrogated by chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by deep sequencing, allowing for quantitative comparison of many mutants in parallel.
evidence: The abstract directly states the method and its capabilities.

claim: Screening of a barcoded yeast knock-out collection for regulators of histone H3K79 methylation by Dot1 identified all known regulators.
source: Screening of a barcoded yeast knock-out collection for regulators of histone H3K79 methylation by Dot1 identified all known regulators as well as novel players and processes.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the screen.

claim: Histone deposition negatively regulates H3K79 methylation.
source: These include histone deposition, homologous recombination, and adenosine kinase, which influences the methionine cycle.
evidence: The abstract lists histone deposition as one of the novel regulators identified.

claim: Homologous recombination negatively regulates H3K79 methylation.
source: These include histone deposition, homologous recombination, and adenosine kinase, which influences the methionine cycle.
evidence: The abstract lists homologous recombination as one of the novel regulators identified.

claim: Adenosine kinase influences H3K79 methylation through its effect on the methionine cycle.
source: These include histone deposition, homologous recombination, and adenosine kinase, which influences the methionine cycle.
evidence: The abstract states adenosine kinase influences the methionine cycle and thereby affects H3K79 methylation.

claim: Gcn5 regulates histone methylation and H2B ubiquitination.
source: Gcn5, the acetyltransferase within the SAGA complex, was found to regulate histone methylation and H2B ubiquitination.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding.

claim: Chromatin is frequently misregulated in cancer.
source: Given the frequent misregulation of chromatin in cancer, it is important to understand the cellular mechanisms that regulate chromatin structure.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Human DOT1L is important in a subset of leukemias that express an MLL fusion protein caused by rearrangements of the MLL gene.
source: Human DOT1L is important in a subset of leukemias that express an MLL fusion protein caused by rearrangements of the MLL gene (MLL-r) (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: DOT1L inhibitors are currently in clinical trials for the treatment of MLL-r leukemia.
source: DOT1L inhibitors have been developed and are currently in clinical trials for the treatment of MLL-r leukemia (Stein and Tallman, 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Ubiquitination of H2B by Bre1 in yeast or RNF20/40 in mammals promotes H3K79 methylation.
source: The best-characterized regulatory pathway is a trans-histone cross-talk: ubiquitination of H2B by Bre1 in yeast or RNF20/40 in mammals promotes H3K79 methylation (Weake and Workman, 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The barcoded knock-out library was created by crossing the NatMX knock-out library with the Barcoder collection.
source: First, we generated a new barcoded yeast knock-out library by crossing a knock-out library that does not contain barcodes (Tong and Boone, 2006), with a Barcoder library (Yan et al., 2008) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text describes the method and Figure 1A illustrates it.

claim: The barcoded library contains approximately 4300 strains divided over five subsets with unique barcodes.
source: We obtained a set of approximately 4300 strains, divided over five subsets with unique barcodes.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the library construction.

claim: Both barcode loci (UpTag and DownTag) showed an intermediate level of H3K79 methylation in a wild-type strain.
source: Both barcode loci showed an intermediate level of H3K79 methylation in a wild-type strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text states this and references a figure showing the data.

claim: The Epi-ID screen identified dot1Δ strains as showing low H3K79me1 and H3K79me3 at both the UpTag and DownTag.
source: The spiked-in controls were clear outliers: dot1Δ strains showed low H3K79me1 and H3K79me3 at both the UpTag and DownTag
evidence: This is stated as a result from the screen.

claim: bre1Δ strains showed low H3K79me3 and high H3K79me1 in the Epi-ID screen.
source: bre1Δ strains showed low H3K79me3 and high H3K79me1
evidence: This is stated as a result from the screen.

claim: Dot1 over-expression strains showed high H3K79me3 and low H3K79me1 in the Epi-ID screen.
source: Dot1 over-expression strains showed high H3K79me3 and low H3K79me1.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the screen.

claim: Rad6 and Lge1 are positive regulators of H3K79 methylation.
source: Positive regulators of H3K79 methylation were Rad6 and Lge1, which form the H2B ubiquitination complex together with Bre1 (Weake and Workman, 2008)
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen with citation support.

claim: Rtf1 is a positive regulator of H3K79 methylation.
source: and Rtf1, which is part of the PAF transcription-elongation complex and recruits Bre1/Rad6 to chromatin of transcribed regions (Piro et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen with citation support.

claim: Deletion of genes encoding Ubp8, Sgf73, Sgf11 and Sus1 led to increased methylation on the UpTag.
source: Ubp8 and its partners in the deubiquitinase (DUB) module of the SAGA complex (Sgf73, Sgf11 and Sus1) together deubiquitinate H2B and predominantly act at the 5' ends of transcribed regions (Bonnet et al., 2014; Morgan et al., 2016; Schulze et al., 2011). In the Epi-ID screen, deletion of the genes encoding these proteins led to increased methylation on the UpTag, but not on the DownTag
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen with citation support for the known function.

claim: No H3K79 demethylases are known.
source: No H3K79 demethylases are known (Sweet et al., 2010; Zee et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The Epi-ID screen provided no evidence of an H3K79 demethylase.
source: and the Epi-ID screen provided no evidence of an H3K79 demethylase either. None of the genes with a known demethylase domain was found among the negative regulators (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen with reference to a figure.

claim: There is a negative correlation between growth rate and H3K79 methylation level.
source: Figure 2A shows a negative correlation between the growth rate and the H3K79 methylation score on both UpTag and DownTag (r = −0.4)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A showing the correlation.

claim: H3K79 methylation was significantly higher for the slow growers than for the remainder of the yeast strains.
source: and methylation was significantly higher for the slow growers than for the remainder of the yeast strains (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A showing the data.

claim: Rtt109 was one of the strongest negative regulators of H3K79 methylation on the UpTag.
source: Rtt109 was one of the strongest negative regulators of H3K79 methylation on the UpTag (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2B showing the data.

claim: High H3K79 methylation upon deletion of RTT109 could be validated by ChIP-qPCR.
source: and high H3K79 methylation upon deletion of RTT109 could be validated by ChIP-qPCR (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2C showing the validation data.

claim: Rtt109 is a histone acetyltransferase that acetylates newly synthesized histone H3 on lysine 56.
source: Rtt109 is a histone acetyltransferase that acetylates newly synthesized histone H3 on lysine 56 (Driscoll et al., 2007; Han et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Rtt109 promotes histone transport and nucleosome assembly through its acetyltransferase activity.
source: Through this activity, Rtt109 promotes histone transport and nucleosome assembly (Dahlin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Nat1 and Ard1 were among the strongest positive regulators of H3K79me on both the UpTag and DownTag.
source: Among the strongest positive regulators of H3K79me on both the UpTag and DownTag were Nat1 and Ard1, the two components of the NatA N-acetyltransferase complex.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen.

claim: Ard1 has been reported to promote H2Bub and specifically H3K79me3.
source: Ard1 has been reported to promote H2Bub and specifically H3K79me3, but the role of Nat1 remained uncertain (Takahashi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Nat1 has an identical effect to Ard1 on H2B ubiquitination and H3K79 methylation.
source: We confirmed the effect of Ard1 on H2B ubiquitination and H3K79 methylation, and found an identical effect for Nat1 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing the data.

claim: H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were decreased in nat1Δ and ard1Δ strains.
source: Also H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were decreased in nat1Δ and ard1Δ strains, and again the effect was partial compared to the bre1Δ strain (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing the data.

claim: H3K36me3 decreases in the absence of H2B ubiquitination.
source: We confirmed the decrease in H3K36me3 in the absence of H2B ubiquitination (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is stated with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: H3K36me2 was not affected by the absence of H2B ubiquitination.
source: and observed that H3K36me2 was not affected.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: The NatA complex is required for a normal H2Bub level and thereby promotes all downstream methylation events.
source: We conclude that the NatA complex is required for a normal H2Bub level and thereby promotes all downstream methylation events.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: ADO1 was a strong positive H3K79me regulator.
source: Another strong positive H3K79me regulator was ADO1. At both the UpTag and DownTag the ado1Δ strain showed very low H3K79 methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen.

claim: Immunoblot analysis confirmed ADO1 as a positive regulator of H3K79 methylation on a global level.
source: Immunoblot analysis confirmed ADO1 as a positive regulator of H3K79 methylation, showing that also on a global level there is a shift from H3K79me3 to H3K79me1 in the ado1Δ strain (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing the validation data.

claim: H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were decreased in ado1Δ cells.
source: In addition, H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were decreased in ado1Δ cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing the data.

claim: H2Bub was not decreased in ado1Δ cells.
source: H2Bub was not decreased in ado1Δ cells (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing the data.

claim: The ADO1 gene encodes yeast adenosine kinase, responsible for phosphorylating adenosine to generate AMP.
source: The ADO1 gene encodes yeast adenosine kinase, responsible for phosphorylating adenosine to generate AMP.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: SAH levels increased 19-fold in the absence of adenosine kinase.
source: As shown in Figure 3D, SAH levels increased 19-fold in the absence of adenosine kinase.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3D showing the measurement data.

claim: SAM levels increased by 75-fold in the absence of adenosine kinase.
source: However, SAM levels increased by as much as 75-fold, causing an unexpected 4-fold increase of the SAM/SAH ratio.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the measurements.

claim: The SAM/SAH ratio increased 4-fold in the absence of adenosine kinase.
source: However, SAM levels increased by as much as 75-fold, causing an unexpected 4-fold increase of the SAM/SAH ratio.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the measurements.

claim: SAH is a known inhibitor of methyltransferases.
source: since SAH is a known inhibitor of methyltransferases (Etchegaray and Mostoslavsky, 2016; Richon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Mms22-Rtt101-Mms1, Slx5-Slx8, and Rad51-Rad57 complexes were enriched among negative regulators and are all involved in DNA repair at replication forks.
source: Strikingly, of the enriched complexes on the UpTag, Mms22-Rtt101-Mms1, Slx5-Slx8, and Rad51-Rad57 were all involved in DNA repair, specifically at replication forks (see below) (Branzei et al., 2006; Costes and Lambert, 2012; Duro et al., 2008; Su et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: PANTHER identified processes enriched among the candidate negative regulators at the UpTag, with the highest enrichment scores for double-strand break repair via homologous recombination and recombinational repair.
source: Second, we used PANTHER (Mi et al., 2016) to identify processes enriched among the candidate negative regulators at the UpTag (Table 2). With the exception of two very general terms, all enriched GO processes fall into the DNA repair category. The highest enrichment scores were found for double-strand break (DSB) repair via homologous recombination (HR) and its parent recombinational repair (Table 2, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Table 2 and Figure 4A showing the analysis results.

claim: ChIP-qPCR showed an increase in methylation at the HO promoter in both slx8Δ and mms21ΔC strains.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, ChIP-qPCR showed an increase in methylation at the HO promoter, near the UpTag, in both slx8Δ and mms21ΔC, implicating the SUMO-ubiquitin pathway in regulating H3K79 methylation.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4B showing the validation data.

claim: A small global increase in methylation was observed in slx8Δ and mms21ΔC strains by mass spectrometry.
source: A small global increase in methylation was observed in these strains by mass spectrometry (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C showing the mass spectrometry data.

claim: SAGA complex subunits were highly enriched among the negative H3K79me regulators on the UpTag.
source: SAGA complex subunits were highly enriched among the negative H3K79me regulators on the UpTag (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Table 1 showing the enrichment analysis.

claim: Gcn5 and its partners in the HAT module, Ada2 and Ngg1 (Ada3), were among the strongest negative regulators.
source: Indeed, Gcn5 and its partners in the HAT module, Ada2 and Ngg1 (Ada3), were among the strongest negative regulators (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2B showing the screen data.

claim: A gcn5Δ strain had more H3K79me3 and less H3K79me1 globally as measured by mass spectrometry.
source: Mass spectrometry measurements demonstrated that the effect of Gcn5 was not limited to the UpTag, since a gcn5Δ strain also had more H3K79me3 and less H3K79me1 globally (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A showing the mass spectrometry data.

claim: The Gcn5-F221A mutant was not able to rescue the knock-out phenotype.
source: In contrast to wild-type Gcn5, the Gcn5-F221A mutant was not able to rescue the knock-out phenotype (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to figures showing the Epi-ID experiment data.

claim: H3K79me regulation by Gcn5 depends on its catalytic activity.
source: This finding suggests that H3K79me regulation by Gcn5 depends on its catalytic activity.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the Gcn5-F221A mutant data.

claim: gcn5Δ strains had significantly more H2Bub on the UpTag than wild-type strains.
source: Indeed, gcn5Δ strains were found to have significantly more H2Bub on the UpTag than wild-type strains, and this was also the case for cells expressing the inactive Gcn5-F221A protein (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5C showing the Epi-ID data.

claim: H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were increased in the absence of Gcn5 acetyltransferase activity.
source: Since H2Bub levels were affected, we also tested the effect on H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 in the custom Epi-ID experiment and found both to be increased in the absence of Gcn5 acetyltransferase activity (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5C showing the Epi-ID data.

claim: An increase in H2Bub and a decrease in H3K9ac could be observed at the HO promoter in gcn5Δ strains by ChIP-qPCR.
source: First, using ChIP-qPCR, both an increase in H2Bub and a decrease in H3K9ac could be observed at the HO promoter, near the UpTag in gcn5Δ strains (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5D showing the ChIP-qPCR data.

claim: Both gcn5Δ and ada2Δ strains showed increased H2Bub levels globally by immunoblotting.
source: Second, immunoblotting was used to determine the global change in H2Bub level. Both gcn5Δ and ada2Δ strains showed increased H2Bub -levels (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement A–C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to figures showing the immunoblot data.

claim: Ubp8 protein expression was significantly decreased in the absence of Gcn5.
source: To investigate this further, we examined the expression of H2Bub regulators and observed that Ubp8 protein expression was significantly decreased in the absence of Gcn5 (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is stated with reference to figures showing the protein expression data.

claim: A reduction in Ubp8 protein level was also observed in chromatin fractions.
source: A reduction in Ubp8 protein level was also observed in chromatin fractions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to a figure showing the chromatin fraction data.

claim: Gcn5 is required for Ubp8 stability, potentially by regulating the association with its partners in the SAGA DUB module.
source: These findings suggest that Gcn5 is required for Ubp8 stability, potentially by regulating the association with its partners in the SAGA DUB module.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the Ubp8 expression data.

claim: Epi-ID can be performed on pools of cells, making it easily applicable to large collections of mutants.
source: First, in contrast to other techniques used to screen for chromatin regulators (Dover et al., 2002; Peng et al., 2008; Schulze et al., 2009), Epi-ID can be performed on pools of cells, making it easily applicable to large collections of mutants.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method with citations to other methods.

claim: Epi-ID is a direct method, in contrast to reporter gene assays.
source: Second, Epi-ID is a direct method, in contrast to reporter gene assays that have been used to read out chromatin changes (Rossmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method with a citation to reporter assays.

claim: Epi-ID is a very sensitive method that is able to pick up differences that cannot be detected by immunoblot.
source: Third, it is a very sensitive method that is able to pick up differences that cannot be detected by immunoblot.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method.

claim: All tested candidate regulators from the Epi-ID screen could be validated on a global level and/or locally by ChIP-qPCR.
source: All tested candidate regulators could be validated on a global level and/or locally, by ChIP-qPCR.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of validation experiments.

claim: The H2Bub-H3K79me trans-histone cross-talk is the main Dot1 regulatory pathway.
source: It is clear from our data that the well-studied H2Bub-H3K79me trans-histone cross-talk is the main Dot1 regulatory pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the screen data.

claim: Histone dilution is the main mechanism to counteract Dot1 activity in the absence of a demethylase.
source: No candidate H3K79 demethylase was identified and histone deposition was found to negatively regulate H3K79 methylation, supporting the hypothesis that in the absence of a demethylase histone dilution is the main mechanism to counteract Dot1 activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the screen data.

claim: Epi-ID is not limited to the use of knock-out collections but is highly flexible with regard to the library being screened.
source: However, Epi-ID is not limited to the use of knock-out collections but is highly flexible with regard to the library being screened.
evidence: This is stated as a discussion of the method's applicability.

claim: The technology can easily be applied to chromatin features other than H3K79 methylation.
source: The technology can easily be applied to chromatin features other than H3K79 methylation. As an example, we showed a small Epi-ID experiment for H2B ubiquitination (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated with an example shown in a figure.

claim: The only requirement for an Epi-ID experiment is that a ChIP against the chromatin feature of interest can pull down one or both of the barcoded regions at the HO locus.
source: The only requirement for an Epi-ID experiment is that a ChIP against the chromatin feature of interest can pull down one or both of the barcoded regions at the HO locus.
evidence: This is stated as a technical requirement of the method.

claim: The concept of Epi-ID is in principle transferable to other organisms.
source: However, the concept of Epi-ID, i.e. barcode-ChIP-seq in mutant backgrounds, is not restricted to yeast and is in principle transferable to other organisms.
evidence: This is stated as a discussion of the method's broader applicability.

claim: Dot1 has a distributive mechanism of methylation.
source: Here it is important to consider Dot1's distributive mechanism of methylation (Frederiks et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: With increasing Dot1 activity, H3K79me1 will first increase and then decrease, as it is being converted into higher methylation states.
source: With increasing Dot1 activity, H3K79me1 will first increase and then decrease, as it is being converted into higher methylation states.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the distributive mechanism.

claim: Deletion of UBP10 did not increase H3K79me on the barcodes.
source: Notably, deletion of the other H2B DUB, UBP10, did not increase H3K79me on the barcodes, consistent with the observation that Ubp10 preferentially acts on telomeres (Gardner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the screen with a citation to support the interpretation.

claim: H3K79 methylation is very stable and accumulates on old histones.
source: H3K79 methylation is very stable and accumulates on old histones (De Vos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: A negative correlation between histone turnover and H3K79me3 level has been observed in genome-wide maps.
source: A negative correlation between histone turnover and H3K79me3 level has been observed in genome-wide maps (Radman-Livaja et al., 2011; Weiner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: It has been proposed that slow-growing cells accumulate more H3K79 methylation based on observations and computational modeling.
source: Based on these observations and computational modeling, it has been proposed that slow-growing cells accumulate more H3K79 methylation (De Vos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: RTT109 deletion directly leads to decreased turnover at 'hot' nucleosomes, mostly found in promoters.
source: RTT109 deletion directly leads to decreased turnover at 'hot' nucleosomes, mostly found in promoters (Dion et al., 2007; Kaplan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Histone turnover is an important determinant of the H3K79me level.
source: The fact that Rtt109 was one of the strongest negative regulators of H3K79me at the UpTag, i.e. in a promoter region, indicates that histone turnover is an important determinant of the H3K79me level.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the Rtt109 data.

claim: The deposition of new histones (replication-coupled or -independent) is an important mechanism to counteract H3K79 methylation.
source: Altogether, these data support the idea that no H3K79 demethylase is active in yeast and show that the deposition of new histones (replication-coupled or -independent) is an important mechanism to counteract H3K79 methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: NatA and Dot1 act in the same silencing pathway.
source: Notably, that NatA acts upstream of Dot1 is in agreement with our previous observation that NatA and Dot1 act in the same silencing pathway (van Welsem et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: Dot1 expression levels are unaltered in nat1Δ and ard1Δ strains.
source: However, no significant decrease in Dot1 and H2B ubiquitination factors or increase in H2Bub deubiquitinating factors was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: This is stated with reference to figures showing the protein expression data.

claim: Clearance of adenosine by Ado1 may indirectly affect the methylation cycle and thereby the methylation potential in the cell.
source: Clearance of adenosine by Ado1 may indirectly affect the methylation cycle and thereby the methylation potential in the cell (Boison, 2013; Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated with a citation and illustrated in a figure.

claim: Disruption of the methionine cycle by genetic perturbation or nutrient supply is known to affect histone methylation in yeast and other organisms.
source: Disruption of the methionine cycle by genetic perturbation or nutrient supply is known to affect histone methylation in yeast and other organisms (Janke et al., 2015; Sadhu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The absolute levels of SAH and SAM are important for methyltransferase activity.
source: Although the SAM/SAH ratio is often considered to determine the activity of methyltransferases (Etchegaray and Mostoslavsky, 2016), our findings suggest that the absolute levels of SAH and SAM are also important.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the SAM/SAH measurement data with a citation.

claim: Slx5 and Slx8 form a heterodimeric SUMO-targeted Ubiquitin Ligase complex (StUbL) that is required to maintain genomic stability.
source: Slx5 and Slx8 form a heterodimeric SUMO-targeted Ubiquitin Ligase complex (StUbL) that is required to maintain genomic stability (Nagai et al., 2008; Xie et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Strains lacking Slx5 or Slx8 grow very slowly due to the amplification of endogenous 2µ circles.
source: Strains lacking Slx5 or Slx8 grow very slowly due to the amplification of endogenous 2µ circles (Burgess et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The substrates of the Slx5/Slx8 StUbL complex largely overlap with those of the SUMO ligase Mms21.
source: Because the substrates of the Slx5/Slx8 StUbL complex largely overlap with those of the SUMO ligase Mms21 (Albuquerque et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Homologous recombination is needed to restart replication forks that have stalled or collapsed in untreated cells.
source: No DNA-damaging agents were present in the Epi-ID experiment. However, also in untreated cells homologous recombination is needed to restart replication forks that have stalled or collapsed, for instance at structure-forming sequences or replication-fork barriers (Costes and Lambert, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Mms22, Rtt101 and Mms1 form a Cul4-like E3 ubiquitin ligase that sits at replication forks and promotes restart of stalled forks.
source: Mms22, Rtt101 and Mms1 (of which Rtt101 was not in the dataset) form a Cul4-like E3 ubiquitin ligase that sits at replication forks and promotes restart of stalled forks, presumably through homologous recombination (Buser et al., 2016; Vaisica et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Rad52 and its partners are central players in homologous recombination, also at replication forks.
source: Rad52 and its partners are central players in homologous recombination, also at replication forks (Costes and Lambert, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The Slx5 and Slx8 StUbL complex and Mms21 promote translocation of DNA breaks and collapsed replication forks to nuclear pores.
source: The Slx5 and Slx8 StUbL complex and Mms21 promote translocation of DNA breaks and collapsed replication forks to nuclear pores (Burgess et al., 2007; Horigome et al., 2016; Su et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Nup84 is required for translocation of DNA breaks and collapsed replication forks to nuclear pores.
source: Interestingly, also the nuclear pore component required for this translocation, Nup84 (Su et al., 2015), was identified as a negative regulator of H3K79me in the Epi-ID screen.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: At the nuclear pore, Slx5/8 modulate homologous recombination by targeting protein substrates for degradation, including Rad52.
source: At the pore, Slx5/8 modulate homologous recombination by targeting protein substrates for degradation, including Rad52 itself (Su et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Sgs1 facilitates re-initiation of stalled replication forks.
source: Other factors from the process of HR-mediated DSB repair that were among the negative regulators (Figure 4A) include Sgs1, which also facilitates re-initiation of stalled replication forks (Ashton and Hickson, 2010)
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Ctf4 tethers Mms22 to the replisome.
source: and Ctf4, which tethers Mms22 to the replisome (Buser et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: H2B ubiquitination facilitates fork recovery.
source: Since H2B ubiquitination has been described to facilitate fork recovery (Lin et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: H2Bub levels were not increased in slx8Δ and mms21ΔC strains.
source: However, H2Bub levels were not increased (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This is stated with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Dot1 expression was not altered in slx5Δ and slx8Δ strains.
source: and neither was Dot1 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Dot1 mediates checkpoint activation and recombinational repair after UV damage.
source: Dot1 has been shown to function in several DNA repair pathways; it mediates checkpoint activation and recombinational repair after UV damage, and represses translesion synthesis (Conde and San-Segundo, 2008; Rossodivita et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Dot1 represses translesion synthesis.
